divergenceFinding.severity: MUST-FIX BEFORE ANY PRODUCTION ROLLBACK IS RELIED UPON
divergenceFinding.statement: DIGEST_AFTER_REAPPLY (c70e119a) does not equal DIGEST_POST_APPLY (09c42928). A rollback followed by a reapply lands on a structurally different catalog than a clean first apply, even though both pass all 286 hosted assertions.
divergenceFinding.whyItHappens_bestSupportedExplanation: The accepted rollbacks are FORWARD-RESTORATION scripts, not exact inverse DDL. The posture they reconstruct is therefore not guaranteed byte-identical to the true pre-03A posture, and reapplying the forward candidates on top of an approximated baseline lands on a stable but different state. The apply MECHANISM is not the cause: DDL semantics do not depend on whether a statement arrived via the Management API or the CLI.
divergenceFinding.whyItCouldNotBeLocalisedExactly: I hashed the original post-apply state but did NOT retain its full structural JSON, so the original cannot be diffed field-by-field. This is my error in checkpoint discipline and is recorded as such rather than hidden.

whatWasLocalised.assessment: Every observed difference in this direction is an intended Phase 03A effect. Nothing anomalous was found in the rolled-back-vs-reapplied comparison itself.
